subject: anatomy
title: Development of the nervous system, eye and ear

steps.tx: The **neural tube** arises from the neural plate by neurulation and gives rise to the entire central nervous system. Its cranial part forms three primary brain vesicles: **prosencephalon**, **mesencephalon** and **rhombencephalon**. The caudal part forms the spinal cord. Closure begins in the future cervical region and spreads both cranially and caudally, finishing around day 27.

steps.tx: The **alar plate** lies dorsally and gives sensory, afferent neurons such as posterior horn cells. The **basal plate** lies ventrally and gives motor, efferent neurons. Visceral efferent columns, which supply cardiac and smooth muscle, arise from the basal plate as lateral horn cells. Anterior horn cells, which supply skeletal muscle, also come from the basal plate.

steps.tx: The **optic vesicle** is an outgrowth of the prosencephalon, so the retina and optic nerve are neuroectodermal. The vesicle invaginates to form the **optic cup**, whose outer thin layer becomes the retinal pigmented epithelium. The **lens placode** is surface ectoderm and forms the lens. Failure of the optic fissure to close produces a **coloboma**.

steps.tx: The **pituitary** has two embryological origins. The anterior lobe, the adenohypophysis, develops from **Rathke pouch**, an ectodermal upgrowth of the stomodeum roof. The posterior lobe, the neurohypophysis, develops from the infundibulum, a downgrowth of the diencephalon floor. A **craniopharyngioma** arising from remnants of Rathke pouch is a classic exam association. The **inner ear** develops from the **otic vesicle** and is adult sized by about 20 to 22 weeks.

steps.tx: Neural tube defects are high yield. Failure of the **rostral neuropore** to close causes **anencephaly**, usually between days 23 and 26. Failure of caudal closure causes **spina bifida**. On ultrasound, spina bifida shows the **lemon sign** and the **banana sign**. The spinal cord ends at L3 in newborns and reaches the adult level around L1, which is why lumbar puncture sites differ with age.
